sentences.text: Shri D.K. Paroha, Ga for the State.
Heard on I.A. No.6597/2022, which is an application filed by the applicants for taking additional documents on record.
The documents are order-sheets of the trial Court showing that the applicants have surrendered before the trial Court.
The application is allowed.
The documents are taken on record.
Heard on admission.
Admit.
Heard on I.A.No. 6201/2022, which is an application for suspension of sentence and grant of bail to the applicants.

The applicants have been convicted by the trial Court under Sections 7(1)(3) (5), 16(1)(A)(I)(II) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act and sentenced to S.I. for six months (on each count) with fine of Rs.500/- (on each count) each, respectively with default stipulation.
The aforesaid conviction and sentence has been affirmed by the lower appellate Court.
Learned counsel for the applicants submits that applicants are in custody.
The maximum sentence awarded to the applicants is of six months.
The applicants are in custody since 4.4.2022.
This revision would take considerable to dispose of finally.
In view of the aforesaid, prayer is made to suspend the jail sentence of the applicants and to release them on bail.
Learned Government Advocate has opposed the application.

Looking to the nature of the offence and the period of sentence awarded to the applicants, without commenting on the merit of the case,
this application is allowed.

It is directed subject to depositing the fine amount, if not already deposited and on furnishing a personal bond in a sum of Rs.40,000/- [Rupees Forty Thousand only] each with one solvent surety Prahlad Singh Sen vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 18 April, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/51068492/

The applicants shall appear before the trial Court concerned on 18.8.2022 and on all subsequent dates as may be fixed in this regard, without fail.
List for final hearing in due course.
